candidate.analysis: Analyze /input/public_csv using only the named CSV. Filter to ethics-focused debates when the topic fields permit, then summarize the target percentage increase by moderator ethical stance and critical-event occurrence. Compute Pearson correlations between argument intensity, audience interest, average debate duration, and number of sessions and the target, plus group means and sample sizes. Print concise observations, while reporting missing or insufficient data instead of inventing conclusions.
candidate.answer: Among 259 ethics-focused debates, argument intensity could not be correlated with the target because it had zero variance or insufficient usable variation. Audience interest, average debate duration, and number of sessions showed negligible correlations with the percentage increase in utilitarianism (r=-0.006, 0.074, and 0.053). Moderator stance was strongly associated: utilitarian moderators averaged 65.189%, versus 0.054% for deontological and 0.570% for virtue-ethics moderators. Critical events were associated with higher increases (29.441% when present versus 6.143% when absent), especially for utilitarian moderators (100.000% with an event versus 25.886% without). These are descriptive associations, not causal conclusions.
